name: health
title: Clinical documentation
summary: Drafts clinical notes and explains care in plain language, without leaking patient details.

skills.name: phi-guard
skills.title: Protect patient privacy
skills.blurb: Replaces names, dates and record numbers before anything is written down.
skills.description: Use before quoting, copying or writing any clinical text, and whenever asked to de-identify a document.
skills.body:
Protected health information never leaves a document it is in unless the task is to move it.

When writing any new file or answer from clinical text:
- Replace each of the HIPAA identifiers with a bracketed placeholder: names become [PATIENT] or [CLINICIAN], dates more specific than the year become [DATE], ages over 89 become [AGE 90+], clinic and hospital names become [FACILITY], and addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, medical record numbers, insurance numbers and any other account or device numbers become [ADDRESS], [PHONE], [EMAIL], [MRN], [INSURANCE ID] and [ID].
- Keep clinical facts, medications, doses and results exactly as written.
- When de-identifying, write a new file beside the original with `-deidentified` before the extension, and list at the end how many of each placeholder you used, as placeholders and counts only.
- If you are not sure whether a string identifies somebody, replace it and say so.
- Your replies follow the same rule. Say what you replaced by its placeholder and never quote the original, not even to explain the change.

skills.name: soap-note
skills.title: Write SOAP notes
skills.blurb: Turns visit notes into a SOAP note, marked for your review.
skills.description: Use when asked for a SOAP note, a progress note or a clinical summary of a visit.
skills.body:
Write the note from the source text alone.

Structure:
- **Subjective**: the patient's own account, history of the present illness, and relevant history, in the source's terms.
- **Objective**: vitals, examination findings and results, with units.
- **Assessment**: only the assessments the clinician recorded. Never add a diagnosis the source does not contain.
- **Plan**: medications with dose, route and frequency; tests ordered; referrals; follow-up; patient education.

Rules:
- Write "not documented" for anything a section needs and the source does not say.
- Apply the phi-guard skill to the note.
- Save it as `soap-note.md` unless told otherwise.
- End with the line: `Draft for clinician review. Not a medical record until signed.`

skills.name: plain-language
skills.title: Explain in plain language
skills.blurb: Rewrites instructions so any patient can follow them.
skills.description: Use when asked to explain clinical instructions to a patient, or to rewrite at a reading level.
skills.body:
Rewrite for a patient at a sixth-grade reading level unless another level is asked for.

- Short sentences, one instruction each. Everyday words; explain any medical term you must keep.
- Keep every dose, time and warning exactly. Never soften a warning.
- Use a numbered list for steps and a short "Call your doctor if" list for warning signs.
- Say what the reading level is and how you checked it.

# Sample clinic folder

files.visit-notes.txt:
VISIT NOTES (invented for demonstration; not a real record)
Patient: Maria Okonkwo   DOB: 03/14/1961   MRN: 44-718-209
Seen: 09/22/2026 by Dr. Samuel Reyes, Riverside Family Clinic, 12 Mill Lane, Springfield

Pt reports 3 days of productive cough, green sputum, fever to 38.6 at home, mild SOB on stairs. No chest pain. Hx T2DM on metformin 1000 mg BID, HTN on lisinopril 10 mg daily. Non-smoker. No recent travel.

Vitals: T 38.2 C, HR 96, BP 138/84, RR 20, SpO2 95% RA.
Exam: crackles R lower base, no wheeze. Otherwise unremarkable.
CXR: R lower lobe consolidation.
A: community-acquired pneumonia, R lower lobe. CURB-65 score 1.
P: amoxicillin 1 g PO TID x 5 days. Paracetamol 1 g PO q6h PRN fever, max 4 g/day. Check glucose twice daily while unwell. Review in clinic in 48 h or sooner if worse.

Discharge instructions given verbally: Take the amoxicillin three times a day with food until all doses are finished, even if you feel better. Drink plenty of fluids. Seek urgent care immediately if breathing becomes more difficult, lips turn blue, confusion develops, or fever persists beyond 72 hours despite antibiotics. Blood sugars may run high during infection; if above 300 mg/dL twice in a row, call the clinic. Phone: 555-0142.
